references.text: The spies fled to the mountains and hid there for three days while their pursuers searched for them, illustrating the outcome of the pursuit that began in verse 7.
Joshua and the Israelites came to the Jordan and camped at the fords, the same fords that the pursuers from Jericho were guarding.
The men of Ephraim took control of the fords across the Jordan toward Moab, highlighting the strategic importance of the Jordan fords also mentioned in Joshua 2:7.
The Gileadites seized the fords across the Jordan toward Ephraim, paralleling how the men of Jericho guarded the fords to capture the spies.
David was advised to cross the Jordan quickly to avoid pursuers, a situation similar to that of the spies in Jericho who were pursued toward the fords.
Jericho was completely shut because of the Israelites; no one went out or came in. This shows that the practice of closing gates for security was common, as also noted in Joshua 2:7.
